findings.title: scheduler request had no one-shot reservation consume or canonical attempt binding
findings.before: prepare-launch accepted a request and attempt directory independently; replaying the request into another canonical-looking directory could start another worker path

findings.title: terminal receipt was not bound to scheduler host/GPU allocation or launch chain
findings.before: finalize_receipt checked only receipt schema, job_id, attempt_id, and execution_status

findings.title: attempt metadata reads followed symlinks and did not enforce a stable single inode
findings.before: collect and worker metadata paths used ordinary pathname reads/open calls

implemented: scheduler binding covers job_id, attempt_id, exact attempt_dir, queue spec hash, reservation id, logical host, host hostname/boot id, and GPU UUID/index
reservation consume uses owner-only O_EXCL creation, fsync, and binding comparison for duplicate/replay handling
probe, prepare-launch, worker, heartbeat, collect, and terminal receipt finalization enforce the same identity chain
worker validates current host boot identity and live GPU UUID/index before launch and during GPU sampling
metadata and receipt reads reject symlink/hardlink/non-regular files and detect inode/stat changes during read

negative_tests: one-shot reservation duplicate and cross-attempt replay
terminal allocation and launch/heartbeat identity mismatch

residual_boundary: This is fail-closed binding and local host/GPU identity checking. It does not claim an independent cryptographic attestation against a same-UID process that can rewrite the trusted runtime or scheduler state; such a trust root is outside core_runtime.py and remains required for production qualification authority.
